explain.say: Imagine working all Saturday morning and getting paid nothing at all, and still smiling! Millions of people do this. Look at the board. It is a circle, because volunteering keeps going round. To volunteer means to give your time to help, by choice and without pay.

faq.a: Volunteering means choosing to give your time and skills to help others or a cause, without being paid. It can be big or small, from a beach clean-up to helping a neighbour.

faq.q: What kinds of volunteering are there?
faq.a: Food banks, clean-ups, tree planting, animal shelters, reading to children, visiting older people, helping at places of worship, and helping during disasters are all common.
It helps people and places in need, like hungry families, lonely older people, animals or the environment, and it gets jobs done that might otherwise be left undone.
Many studies link volunteering with better mood, less loneliness and a sense of purpose. Some people call the warm feeling the helper's high.

faq.a: When people see others helping, they are more likely to help too. Volunteers also invite friends and family, so the effort grows.

facts: The Golden Temple's langar in Amritsar serves free meals to tens of thousands of people daily, cooked and served largely by volunteers.
The UN marks International Volunteer Day every year on 5 December.
The UN's 2022 State of the World's Volunteerism Report estimated about 860 million people aged 15 and over volunteer each month.
